scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 35-45, at a laptop at a desk, cardigan, half a coffee. Screen glow on her face. Delivery is dry and investigative — the register of someone who enjoys catching brands out and is mildly annoyed to have failed.
scripts.hook: I tried to find out where this brand actually makes things. I expected a warehouse in Shenzhen.
scripts.first_frame: Over-shoulder on a laptop showing a map zoomed to northern Norway, her hand on the trackpad.

beats.vo: I tried to find out where this brand actually makes things. I expected a warehouse in Shenzhen.
beats.visual: Over-shoulder, laptop, map of northern Norway on screen.

beats.vo: Instead there's a woman called Line, she's their head of brand, and she writes from a farm inside the Arctic circle.
beats.visual: She turns the laptop toward camera, scrolling the brand's own page.

beats.vo: Which matters less as a story and more as a reason the formulas are what they are — sea buckthorn, arnica, rosehip. Plants that have to survive up there.
beats.visual: Cut to the day balm jar on the desk beside the coffee, opened.

beats.vo: It's a balm, not a cream. Studies show 22% younger skin, and 95% reported youthful glow.
beats.visual: She takes a small amount, presses it into the back of her hand, shows the finish.

beats.vo: Thirty dollars. I went looking for a reason not to buy it and came back with the opposite.
beats.visual: Laptop closed, jar in frame, she shrugs at camera.

beats.vo: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm, from Frøya. Go and check them yourself.
beats.visual: Jar held to camera, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm, from Frøya. Go and check them yourself.
scripts.attribution_basis: angle=heritage_origin (single_brand, 4 ads across Froya Organics). Agent 2 does not carry hook ids through from hooks.jsonl, so DESIGN.md §2 hook-level attribution is INCOMPLETE — traceable to the angle, not to individual ads. Evidence grade copy_derived.

scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 58-68, outdoors on a cold bright day, coat zipped, wind moving her hair. Handheld, slightly unsteady. Delivery is warm and unhurried with the cadence of someone used to being listened to.
scripts.hook: Cold does two things to skin and only one of them is bad.
scripts.first_frame: Outdoors, overcast bright light, her face fills the left of frame with bare landscape behind. Breath faintly visible.

beats.vo: Cold does two things to skin and only one of them is bad.
beats.visual: Outdoors, wind, handheld. She squints slightly against the light.

beats.vo: It strips you. But the plants that grow in it get dense — they concentrate, because they have to.
beats.visual: She gestures at the landscape behind her, camera follows loosely.

beats.vo: That's the whole idea behind this one. Arctic arnica, in a beeswax balm, made for the eye area.
beats.visual: Small jar produced from a coat pocket, held in a gloved hand.

beats.vo: Six of the ten top anti-age ingredients, and it looks less puffy in 4 to 9 days.
beats.visual: Ring finger tapping along the orbital bone, outdoors, no mirror.

beats.vo: Fifty-two dollars, and it's the one I take when I know I'll be out in weather.
beats.visual: She pockets the jar, pulls her collar up.

beats.vo: Magic Revive Eye Balm. Frøya. Made where the weather is worse than here.
beats.visual: Wide shot of her walking away, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Magic Revive Eye Balm. Frøya. Made where the weather is worse than here.
scripts.attribution_basis: angle=heritage_origin (single_brand, 4 ads across Froya Organics). Agent 2 does not carry hook ids through from hooks.jsonl, so DESIGN.md §2 hook-level attribution is INCOMPLETE — traceable to the angle, not to individual ads. Evidence grade copy_derived.

scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 30-40, bathroom, hair clipped up, mid-routine with a wet face. Fast, chatty delivery, slightly amused. She is the youngest avatar in this set on purpose — heritage as craft appeal rather than age appeal.
scripts.hook: Read the ingredients on your scrub. Mine used to be plastic and apricot dust.
scripts.first_frame: Close on her holding a generic scrub tube, squinting at the back-of-pack ingredients, face already wet.

beats.vo: Read the ingredients on your scrub. Mine used to be plastic and apricot dust.
beats.visual: She turns a generic tube to read the back, pulls a face.

beats.vo: This one is arctic rose petal. That's it, that's the abrasive. Rose petal.
beats.visual: Opens the Frøya scrub, tips some into her palm so the texture is visible.

beats.vo: It's rougher than you expect and gentler than it looks, which is a weird combination to describe and easy to feel.
beats.visual: Macro on the scrub between her fingertips.

beats.vo: Skin cells revive in 2 to 9 days. Instant deep and natural cleanse. That's their language, not mine.
beats.visual: She works it over her cheeks in small circles, water running.

beats.vo: Thirty-seven dollars, and I've stopped keeping the plastic one under the sink as a backup.
beats.visual: Rinsing, patting dry with a towel, no reveal shot.

beats.vo: Ultra Cleanse and Revive Face Scrub, from Frøya. Go and read your current one.
beats.visual: Jar on the edge of the sink, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Ultra Cleanse and Revive Face Scrub, from Frøya. Go and read your current one.

scripts.product: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin ($121.07)
scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 50-56, mid-length hair she clearly does herself, sitting on the edge of a bed still in work clothes. Evening lamp light, slightly warm and dim. Delivery is flat and a bit tired — the tone of someone saying a thing out loud for the first time, not performing a realisation.
scripts.hook: Nobody sat me down and told me my face was going to change too.
scripts.first_frame: Mid-shot, woman on the edge of a bed, lamp behind her. She is looking slightly off-camera, not smiling. No product anywhere in frame.

beats.vo: Nobody sat me down and told me my face was going to change too.
beats.visual: Static mid-shot, lamp light. She holds the look for a beat before continuing.

beats.vo: They mention the temperature thing. The sleep thing. Nobody mentions that your skin stops behaving like your skin.
beats.visual: She glances down, back up. Small shrug.

beats.vo: Everything I owned was suddenly wrong. Light lotions sat on top. Foundation went into places it never used to go.
beats.visual: Cut to a cluttered bathroom shelf of half-used bottles, shot plainly from above.

beats.vo: What actually worked for me was going heavier. Balms, not lotions. Norwegian arctic plants, four steps, morning and night.
beats.visual: She sets the four Frøya jars on the bed beside her, unhurried, no flourish.

beats.vo: It supports the skin barrier in 7 days, and 95% reported youthful glow. I mostly just stopped feeling like my face was a stranger.
beats.visual: Close on her pressing the day balm into her cheek, no mirror.

beats.vo: If your skin changed and nobody warned you either — this is the one I'd hand you.
beats.visual: She holds the system box at chest height. Brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: If your skin changed and nobody warned you either — this is the one I'd hand you.
claims_used: supports the skin barrier in 7 days
scripts.attribution_basis: angle=menopause_skin (UNCLAIMED, 0 corpus hits). No hooks exist to attribute to: the angle is defined by absence, verified by probe regex. Evidence grade copy_derived. Traceable to the angle only, not to any ad.

scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 54-62, filmed by a friend rather than selfie-style, standing in a kitchen mid-conversation with a tea towel still in one hand. Natural daylight. Delivery is brisk and funny, the register of complaining to a mate rather than confiding.
scripts.hook: Three things changed at once and only one of them gets talked about.
scripts.first_frame: Woman standing in a kitchen, caught mid-gesture, tea towel in hand. Slightly off-centre framing — clearly someone else is holding the phone.

beats.vo: Three things changed at once and only one of them gets talked about.
beats.visual: She holds up a finger, kitchen daylight, friend-shot framing.

beats.vo: Sleep. Temperature. And my skin, which went from oily-if-anything to tight by ten in the morning.
beats.visual: She counts them off on her fingers, unpolished.

beats.vo: I kept buying the same thin serums I'd used for twenty years and wondering why nothing landed.
beats.visual: Quick cut: a drawer pulled open, full of small bottles.

beats.vo: Switched to a beeswax balm at night. Rosehip and marigold. It works overnight while you sleep, and it softens the look of fine lines.
beats.visual: She scoops the night balm, warms it between fingers so the texture stretches.

beats.vo: Thirty-seven quid and it's the only thing in that drawer I've rebought.
beats.visual: Jar in palm, label readable, kitchen behind.

beats.vo: Frøya's Wrinkle Smoothing Night Balm. Go heavier than you think you need to.
beats.visual: She tosses the tea towel over her shoulder, jar on the counter. Brand on screen.

scripts.cta: Frøya's Wrinkle Smoothing Night Balm. Go heavier than you think you need to.
claims_used: softens the look of fine lines
scripts.attribution_basis: angle=menopause_skin (UNCLAIMED, 0 corpus hits). No hooks exist to attribute to: the angle is defined by absence, verified by probe regex. Evidence grade copy_derived. Traceable to the angle only, not to any ad.

scripts.product: Complete System For Mature Hair & Scalp ($67.77)
scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 48-55, bathroom, hair wet and pushed back so the hairline and parting are plainly visible. No makeup. Delivery is quiet and matter-of-fact, slightly guarded — this is the vulnerable one and it must not be played for sympathy.
scripts.hook: The hair thing is the part I didn't want to say out loud.
scripts.first_frame: Close on a wet parting, shot from slightly above, bathroom light. Her hands are lifting the hair to show the scalp.

beats.vo: The hair thing is the part I didn't want to say out loud.
beats.visual: Hands lifting wet hair at the parting, scalp visible, unglamorous.

beats.vo: The skin changes, fine, everyone jokes about that. The shedding is the one that got me.
beats.visual: She lets the hair fall, looks at the camera for the first time.

beats.vo: This is a three-step thing. Rosemary shampoo, a rosemary spray, and a serum for the roots.
beats.visual: Three bottles lined up on the edge of the sink, one at a time.

beats.vo: It's made for women whose hair changed with stress, postpartum, perimenopause or menopause. That's the actual brief on the box.
beats.visual: She turns the box so the copy is legible, holds it steady.

beats.vo: Sixty-day supply, sixty-eight dollars. 93% experience better hair. I'm not going to oversell it beyond that.
beats.visual: Massaging the serum into the parting, fingers working the scalp.

beats.vo: Frøya's Complete System for Mature Hair and Scalp. Say it out loud sooner than I did.
beats.visual: Three bottles on the sink, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Frøya's Complete System for Mature Hair and Scalp. Say it out loud sooner than I did.
claims_used: made for women whose hair has been affected by stress, postpartum changes, perimenopause, or menopause
scripts.attribution_basis: angle=menopause_skin (UNCLAIMED, 0 corpus hits). No hooks exist to attribute to: the angle is defined by absence, verified by probe regex. Evidence grade copy_derived. Traceable to the angle only, not to any ad.

scripts.product: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin ($121.07)
scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 45-55, sitting on a sofa late evening, one lamp on, phone propped on a cushion. Slightly slumped posture, no makeup, glass of water beside her. Delivery is slow and thoughtful with real pauses — this angle dies if it is performed briskly.
scripts.hook: My face is the first place my week shows up. Before I notice it anywhere else.
scripts.first_frame: Woman on a sofa in low lamp light, phone-height framing, half her face in shadow. Nothing else in frame.

beats.vo: My face is the first place my week shows up. Before I notice it anywhere else.
beats.visual: Static low-light sofa shot. She holds still, no gesture.

beats.vo: Bad sleep, too much on, not enough water — it's on me by Wednesday and I can see it.
beats.visual: She touches under one eye briefly, not theatrically.

beats.vo: I stopped treating that as a thing to cover and started treating it as information.
beats.visual: Cut to her setting the four jars out on the coffee table in a row.

beats.vo: The routine isn't the fix for a bad week. It's the thing that means a bad week doesn't compound.
beats.visual: Applying the night balm, slow, in lamp light.

beats.vo: Four steps, arctic plants, supports the skin barrier in 7 days. Sixty days or your money back, which is how long it actually takes to tell.
beats.visual: The four jars on the table, shot from above.

beats.vo: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin. Frøya. Listen to your face a bit earlier than I did.
beats.visual: She turns the lamp off. Brand name on screen over black.

scripts.cta: The Complete System for Mature Women's Skin. Frøya. Listen to your face a bit earlier than I did.

results in 60 days or your money back

scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 38-48, getting ready in a hallway mirror before work, jacket half on, moving. Handheld, a bit rushed. Delivery is quick and clipped, talking while doing — the opposite energy to script 01 on the same angle deliberately.
scripts.hook: I can tell you exactly how last week went by looking at my cheeks.
scripts.first_frame: Hallway mirror, she is putting one arm into a jacket, face visible in reflection. Morning light through a door behind.

beats.vo: I can tell you exactly how last week went by looking at my cheeks.
beats.visual: Mirror reflection, jacket half on, movement in frame.

beats.vo: Dull means I didn't sleep. Tight means I lived on coffee. It's a readout, not a mystery.
beats.visual: She leans closer to the mirror, turns her face side to side.

beats.vo: So the morning one has to actually do something in the ninety seconds I give it.
beats.visual: Grabs the day balm from a shelf by the door, opens it one-handed.

beats.vo: Sea buckthorn and pomegranate balm. 95% reported youthful glow. Goes on like a balm, sits like nothing.
beats.visual: Quick press into both cheeks, no blending ritual, finish visible in the mirror.

beats.vo: Under thirty dollars, and it's the only step I don't skip when I'm late.
beats.visual: Jar back on the shelf, she picks up keys.

beats.vo: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm. Frøya. Your face is already telling you — go on.
beats.visual: Door opening, light flare, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Anti-Age and Insane Glow Day Balm. Frøya. Your face is already telling you — go on.

scripts.product: Dry and Itchy Balm for Face and Body ($44.00)
scripts.avatar_brief: Woman 40-52, sitting on the floor against a radiator in winter, jumper sleeves pushed up showing dry forearms. Cold blue daylight. Delivery is plain and unembarrassed, the tone of stating a fact about her own body without apology.
scripts.hook: Every winter my arms tell me the heating's been on for three weeks before I work it out.
scripts.first_frame: Close on a forearm against a jumper sleeve, dry patches visible in cold daylight. No face yet.

beats.vo: Every winter my arms tell me the heating's been on for three weeks before I work it out.
beats.visual: Macro on dry forearm skin, cold window light, sleeve pushed up.

beats.vo: Same signal every year. Indoor air, hot showers, and I notice it on my body before my face.
beats.visual: Pull back to reveal her sitting against a radiator.

beats.vo: This is chamomile and thistle in beeswax. It's for face and body, which is the only reason I actually use it on both.
beats.visual: She opens the jar, scoops with two fingers, texture visible.

beats.vo: Soothes dry, itchy skin. Supports the skin barrier in 7 days. Gentle enough for the face.
beats.visual: Working it into the forearm, then briefly along the jaw.

beats.vo: Forty-four dollars and one jar does both, which is why it's the one that lasts in this house.
beats.visual: Jar set on the radiator shelf, sleeve pulled back down.

beats.vo: Dry and Itchy Balm, from Frøya. When your arms start telling you, believe them.
beats.visual: Wide of her by the window, brand name on screen.

scripts.cta: Dry and Itchy Balm, from Frøya. When your arms start telling you, believe them.

gentle enough for face and body
